example_quote: The Global Private Assets Fund targets a net return of 10-12% p.a.*

value_content: Long-term target allocation ranges by investment type, strategy and geography, printed as percent ranges (10-20%, 35-50%, 50-70%) or point percentages (60%, 25%, 10%, 5%) attached as callout labels to donut charts.
example_value: Investment Type: Direct Credit 10-20%, Direct Equity 35-50%, Secondary 35-50%. Strategy: Buyout 50-70%, Venture/Growth 15-35%, Credit 10-20%. Geography: North America 60%, Europe 25%, APAC 10%, ROW 5%
example_quote: The Fund’s long-term target allocations to these categories are presented below:
txt_failure_mode: The four donut charts and every one of their callout labels are vector graphics with no extractable text layer: pdfplumber returns ZERO characters for the entire 'Target Portfolio Construction' block. The TXT goes straight from 'are presented below:' to the next line '14. What is the fund's maximum capacity?'. All ten allocation figures are invisible to Round 1 - there is not even a hint that a table exists. A related artefact on p23 leaves orphan footnote markers '1 SF IV-V' and '2 SF I-V' with no chart to attach them to.

value_content: Name / Title / Role-Department grid, one row per committee member, ~40 rows. Title and department cells routinely wrap to 2-3 lines.
example_value: Brian Gildea | Head of Evergreen Portfolios | Evergreen Portfolio Management
example_quote: Evergreen Portfolio / Brian Gildea Head of Evergreen Portfolios / Management
txt_failure_mode: Any row whose cell wraps is torn apart. 'Evergreen Portfolio Management' is emitted as 'Evergreen Portfolio' on the line BEFORE the Brian Gildea row and 'Management' on the line after, so the department is orphaned above and below the name. Tom Kerr's title is worse: 'Co-Head of Investments, Head of Secondary' precedes his name line and 'Investments' follows it, while his department 'Secondaries' sits inline. Roughly a third of the 40 rows are affected, and the single-line rows and torn rows are indistinguishable from the token stream.

value_content: Named individual whose departure triggers a suspension, with the consequence spelled out (pause new investments, cease investing, LP replacement vote window).
example_value: Andy Weiner; on death or disability the Company pauses all new investments and all closings until a replacement is elected
example_quote: of the Manager, whether as a result of his death or disability or any other reason, the Company shall pause all new investments in Assets and all closings of the Offerings unless and until a replacement for Mr. Weiner is identified and elected as the manager of the Manager

value_content: Subscribing investor's full legal name. In this family it is almost never a filled value: it is a ruled blank in model/template subscription forms, a bracketed placeholder in sample side letters ('[Board]', '[Investor]'), or held in a Schedule A that was not released.
example_value: (blank ruled line)
example_quote: Name of the Applicant (insert full legal name of Applicant)
txt_failure_mode: Schedule 1 is a 3-column form (item number | bold label + italic instruction | ruled answer line). pdfplumber DROPS the entire item-number column - the numerals 1. through 9. are absent from the TXT - and collapses the ruled answer line into a run of underscores placed after the label's first line, so 'Name of the Applicant' and its answer rule and the italic instruction all interleave. A reader cannot tell from TXT whether the line is blank or filled, nor which ordinal field it is. In SRC004 the equivalent data lives in 'SCHEDULE A ... Name, Address and Subscription of Partners', which is listed in the TOC but is not in the 62-page release at all.

value_content: The investor's subscribed commitment in USD, written onto a ruled blank on the execution page and again on the GP's acceptance clause. Blank in every sampled file.
txt_failure_mode: The execution page is a 2-column signature block and pdfplumber welds the columns: the left-column 'Subscription Amount: $______' line is joined to the right column's ruled 'Print Name of Entity' line, and the very next TXT line reads 'Dated: , ____ By: ______________________________' - the left column's Dated blank fused to the right column's By: signature rule. On an executed copy the subscription amount, the date and the signer's name would land on shared lines and be attributable to the wrong label. SRC005 p12 has the same shape ('a Commitment of [US Dollars] __________________').

value_content: A section heading that is present with its body removed, or an exhibit tab page with no exhibit behind it. The absence is the datum: it tells the pipeline that a null is real, not an extraction miss.
example_value: '5. Compensation.' heading present, entire body blank; Exhibit C divider page carries 8 characters and no fee schedule
example_quote: 5. Compensation.
txt_failure_mode: Both channels agree here, which is the point. TXT for p5 shows the heading followed only by stray scanner artifacts, and the rendered image confirms the rest of the page is genuinely empty white space; p38 is a tab page reading only 'EXHIBITC' with Exhibit D starting on p39. The management fee for this mandate is withheld, not missed. Round 1 can flag it, but only the image proves it rather than suspecting a text-extraction failure.

value_content: The page number printed in the footer, which in this family regularly disagrees with the physical PDF page because of front matter and restarting exhibit numbering ('Page 5 of 16' inside a 48-page PDF; '-24-' on physical page 29; 'MEMORANDUM - 10' on physical page 13).
example_value: Printed footer 'CONFIDENTIAL PRIVATE PLACEMENT MEMORANDUM - 10' on physical PDF page 13 (offset 3)
example_quote: ROCKSTEP HOMETOWN AMERICA FUND I LLC CONFIDENTIAL PRIVATE PLACEMENT MEMORANDUM - 10
txt_failure_mode: The footer text extracts fine; the hazard is semantic. Citations that quote a printed page number will not resolve against the physical page the TXT block header uses, and SRC612 is the worst case (its body footers count to 16 while the PDF runs to 48, so 'Page 5 of 16' and physical page 5 coincide by accident and then diverge). Capture both numbers per page or every downstream page citation in this family is ambiguous.
